Apple Photos喺iOS 27入面有好多令人興奮嘅更新，包括我喺呢個app入面最鍾意嘅功能之一：iCloud共享相簿。

iOS 27 brings several welcome upgrades to shared albums in Apple Photos

Apple's Photos app is one of the apps I use the most, and I bet plenty of iPhone users feel the same way. Photos and videos, screenshots, images friends have shared — they're all stored there.

But did you know the Photos app actually has a social media-like feature too?

I'm not a huge fan of social media, but I do enjoy having a more private, lightly social way to share memories with friends and family. iCloud Shared Albums delivers exactly that.

With iCloud Shared Albums, you can create an album that only shares with people you select. Invitees can add their own photos and videos, and you'll be notified when they do. You can also "like" and comment on shared photos and videos, making it a proper social network of sorts.

I've been using Shared Albums for a long time now and have generally enjoyed the feature, but always felt there were a few areas that needed upgrading. Luckily, iOS 27 finally brings those improvements.

In iOS 27, Shared Albums now support full-resolution photos and videos. A big item on my wishlist has finally been checked off.

Additionally, iOS 27 expands how you can react to photos or videos. Now you can choose any emoji to react with, instead of being limited to just "likes."

Android and Windows users can now participate in album content via the web for the first time. Previously, they could only view what Apple users shared.

Apple has also made it easier to save shared photos — just one tap and you're done. You can also set new participant permissions, and you can opt to have an album expire after a specific date.

These upgrades address all my previous complaints about Shared Albums. Combined with the other changes in iOS 27, it's a big year for Apple Photos.

Do you use iCloud Shared Albums in Apple Photos? Let us know in the comments.
